A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Repo2Run work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching the renumbered empirical study, implementation details and baseline settings.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on 420 Python repositories, component ablations, a developer study and industry-repository evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds a test-pass-rate comparison on 50 repositories in Appendix E, Table 8.

M1.justification: The dual-environment architecture, build/record pipeline, rollback mechanism, dependency tools, base-image switching and Dockerfile synthesis rules remain unchanged in Section 3 and the corresponding appendices.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 420-repository Python benchmark, its domains, the developer study and industry-repository evaluation. The new analysis samples 50 repositories from the existing benchmark without adding a domain or environment-building task.

E2.justification: pipreqs, LLM generator and SWE-agent remain the evaluated baselines. The new pass-rate comparison uses this same set; newly cited agents are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a protocol using 50 randomly sampled repositories, entire-test-suite execution, manually recorded pass rates and thresholds from 10% through 100%. The original benchmark protocol, model, temperature and DGSR/EBSR metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new Appendix E analysis checks whether Repo2Run's advantage persists across test-pass thresholds, supplementing the executability assessment. Existing component ablations, failure analyses, action-frequency analysis and developer study are retained.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 newly explains that repeated experiments sufficient to obtain error bars were not conducted because of time and cost. This adds reporting about repetition and uncertainty, without specifying run counts, seeds or new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds pass-rate results: all tests pass in 17/50 repositories for Repo2Run, 5/50 for SWE-agent, 7/50 for LLM generator and 2/50 for pipreqs. Existing benchmark, ablation and appendix results remain unchanged, including Repo2Run's 361/420 environment-building successes.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same environment-state, transition, building-process and verification definitions and equations. No theorem, proof, formal assumption or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty, scalable environment-building and performance claims. The added appendix evaluation supplies supporting evidence without redefining these main contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E expands the justification for EBSR by explaining that code and test bugs can cause failures independently of environment configuration. It also interprets the new pass-rate results as evidence of correct environments. Section 5.4's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The new checklist adds documentation pointers for repository-hosted LLM prompts, README usage instructions and dependency/licensing information, plus study-approval and working-hours disclosures. These are additional disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changed code availability or implementation settings.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds citations including MarsCode Agent, Trae Agent, RepoMaster and GitTaskBench, expands the repository-level research context and adds support for limitations of configuration tools. The central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The related-work subsections exchange order, and acknowledgements, a NeurIPS checklist and the test-pass appendix are added. There are limited wording, contact and conference-header edits; the main scientific narrative is largely retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 8 and a title logo, corrects ECSR to EBSR in Tables 1 and 3, and reflows and renumbers later appendix material. Existing figures and most table structures retain their designs.

improvement.justification: Appendix E/Table 8 adds useful evidence about passing tests beyond v3's executability and Dockerfile-lint results, while the checklist makes the absence of repeated-run uncertainty explicit. The gain is limited: the new study covers 50 repositories without reported uncertainty or sample identities, and its interpretation as establishing correct environments exceeds what pass rates alone demonstrate.
